title: Evaluation on retracts and extension of a perfect pairing
statement:
Rational evaluation and biduality restrict to split idempotents.
If a pairing $b:K\otimes L\to\omega$ has isomorphisms as
both adjoints $K\to DL$ and $L\to DK$, and idempotents
on its two factors are adjoint under $b$, its restriction to
their images again has both adjoints isomorphisms. This property
is preserved by finite scalar extension. In particular it holds
for Verdier evaluation $DK\otimes K\to\omega$ and its
retracts. For a site-perfect complex, the usual perfect pairing
with its tensor dual to the coefficient unit also restricts and
extends in this way.

proof.text: Obtain full internal-Hom closure from rational operations, specializing its arbitrary FieldStage to E and the identity coefficient embedding. Chosen splittings are already hypotheses; no idempotent-completeness existence theorem is needed.

Use completed transpose naturality and signed-symmetry naturality to identify the adjoint of b(i tensor j) with i followed by the adjoint of b followed by Hom(j,W). Transpose the adjoint-idempotent equation. The inverse of the restricted first adjoint is Hom(q,W) followed by the inverse adjoint and p; the two products reduce by intertwining and the splitting identities. Swap the pairing and repeat for its second adjoint.

The transpose of canonical evaluation is identity. Its restricted transpose is Hom(p,W) followed by Hom(i,W), hence identity by i followed by p equals identity. Injectivity of transposition gives the evaluation restriction equation.

Use the two normalized Verdier adjoint equations. They are isomorphisms because e and the recorded biduality are isomorphisms; involutivity cancels the two swaps. Evaluation naturality precomposed by i tensor identity gives restriction. Naturality of bidual.hom and bidual.inv followed by the split projection gives both displayed restriction formulas.
The first adjoint of unit evaluation is identity. The site-perfect coefficient bidual theorem gives invertibility of its second adjoint.

For every finite coefficient embedding, scalar transpose compatibility writes the first extended adjoint as scalar extension of the old adjoint followed by the specified Hom comparison. Both are isomorphisms. The symmetry square gives the same calculation for the other adjoint. Apply the general retract result over F as well and assemble the conclusion.
